William Makepeace Thackeray, Vanity Fair.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/william-makepeace-thackeray/vanity-fair

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- William Makepeace Thackeray, the author, died 1863.

First publication of the text used: Vanity Fair was published in 1848 by William Makepeace Thackeray.

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1848, before 1931. Standard Ebooks states that the text is in the United States public domain (quoted below). A work published in 1848 enters the United States public domain on 1 January 1944.
- Country of origin: the country of first publication is not in the facts file. The possible countries are the United Kingdom, Ireland, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, India and South Africa. Each of them has a term of life + 70 years or less. The last person to die died in 1863, which is before 1956, so the text is public domain in each of these countries, whichever one is the country of origin, and a simultaneous publication in two of them changes nothing.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
